added.title: Environmental Compliance Manager
added.description:
RahrBSG is looking for a Environmental Compliance Manager in Shakopee, Minnesota. The Environmental Compliance Manager leads environmental compliance and sustainability programs across Rahr Corporation and its subsidiaries, ensuring adherence to federal, state, provincial, and local environmental regulations. As the organization's environmental subject matter expert, this role provides strategic oversight for permitting, compliance assurance, environmental risk management, and environmental management systems, with a strong focus on air quality, water, wastewater, stormwater, waste, and chemical management programs. Partnering closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, and business leaders, the Environmental Compliance Manager supports operational excellence, protects the company's ability to operate, and advances long-term business growth through proactive environmental stewardship and risk reduction.

BENEFITS & PERKS:

Competitive Starting Base Salary between $120,000 - $140,000 annually 

Annual Bonus

Medical benefits with coverage paid for at 90%

Dental and Vision Programs

Generous Annual 401(k) Company Contribution of 15%

Employee Assistance Program

Paid Life Insurance

Short Term Disability

Long Term Disability

Tuition Reimbursement

Generous PTO

Sick Time

12 Paid Company Holidays

Parental Leave

Career Growth and Progression Paths

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Environmental Compliance Leadership

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of corporate environmental compliance programs.

Monitor and interpret environmental regulations and communicate compliance obligations to business leaders.

Ensure facilities maintain compliance with all applicable environmental permits, licenses, registrations, plans, and approvals.

Provide strategic guidance and technical expertise to site leadership regarding environmental risks, regulatory requirements, permitting obligations, and compliance strategies.

Develop environmental standards, procedures, and best practices applicable across all operating companies.

Manage 3rd Party Consultants and Attorneys

Provide options for compliance paths to management

Review permits, amendments and cap-ex additions for compliance and defensibility

Remain current on environmental regulatory initiatives, enforcement trends, emphasis programs, and emerging issues to proactively assess impacts on business operations and compliance obligations

Permitting and Regulatory Management

Lead environmental permitting strategies for new capital projects, facility expansions, and operational changes.

Oversee environmental permit applications, modifications, renewals, registrations, and compliance certifications.

Serve as corporate lead for air permitting, wastewater permitting, stormwater permitting, and waste-related regulatory obligations.

Interface directly with regulatory agencies, consultants, attorneys, and external stakeholders.

Support agency inspections, audits, information requests, and enforcement actions as required.

Coordinate environmental compliance reporting and regulatory submissions.

Develop an internal audit program for compliance related tasks

Air Quality and Emissions Management

Provide technical oversight for emissions inventories, source testing, monitoring programs, and emissions calculations.

Evaluate operational and capital projects for permitting implications and environmental compliance impacts.

Coordinate with engineering and operations teams to identify permitting requirements associated with process modifications.

Maintain documentation supporting compliance with permit requirements and regulatory obligations.

Provide technical leadership for air permitting and regulatory applicability determinations, including BACT, NSR, PSD, and related permitting evaluations, to support business growth while maintaining environmental compliance.

Environmental Management Systems

Develop and maintain corporate environmental management systems (EMS).

Establish environmental metrics, KPIs, and performance indicators.

Support ISO 14001 implementation and continuous improvement initiatives.

Develop compliance calendars and audit protocols.

Maintain environmental records management systems and compliance tracking tools.

Sustainability and Stewardship

Support corporate sustainability initiatives and environmental performance improvement projects.

Identify opportunities to reduce emissions, waste generation, water usage, and overall environmental impact.

Assist with environmental data collection and reporting initiatives.

Partner with business leaders to support sustainability objectives and strategic environmental goals.

Act as point of contact for customer’s sustainability related requests

Training and Leadership

Develop and deliver environmental compliance training programs.

Participate in capital project reviews and Management of Change (MOC) processes.

Build a culture of environmental ownership and accountability throughout the organization.

Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the company and operational needs.

MINIMUM EDUCATION & WORK REQUIREMENTS: 

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Management, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.

6+ years of progressive environmental compliance experience in manufacturing, food processing, agricultural processing, energy production, chemical processing, or other industrial environments.

Multi-site environmental management experience strongly preferred.

Demonstrated experience overseeing environmental permitting and regulatory compliance programs.

Experience working directly with environmental regulatory agencies and environmental consultants.

Preferred Certifications

Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)

Certified Environmental Professional (CEP)

Professional Engineer (PE)

ISO 14001 Auditor Training

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, and ABILITIES:

Advanced knowledge of federal, state, provincial, and local environmental regulations.

Strong knowledge of environmental regulatory compliance programs, including the Clean Air Act (CAA), wastewater treatment and discharge requirements, industrial stormwater permitting, Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) regulations, Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA), Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), chemical management, and spill prevention and response programs.

Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple environmental compliance initiatives, regulatory deadlines, documentation requirements, and cross-functional priorities while maintaining accuracy, accountability, and timely execution.

Demonstrated ability to manage complex environmental projects and compliance initiatives.

Ability to interpret technical regulations and communicate requirements to non-technical audiences.

Effective verbal and written communication skills.

Ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders.

Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

Experience with environmental reporting systems, SharePoint, Microsoft Office Suite, and compliance management platforms.

RahrBSG is a family-owned global leader and trusted partner to the craft beverage industry, proudly supporting breweries, wineries, distilleries, cideries, and storefronts with premium supplies and ingredients since 1847. With over 175 years of expertise, RahrBSG combines tradition with innovation to meet the evolving needs of our customers and the craft beverage community.

Headquartered in Shakopee, MN, RahrBSG is part of Rahr Corporation, a fifth-generation family business. We are committed to providing the highest quality products and services to our customers, ensuring they can create beverages that inspire and delight. Our offerings include an extensive range of barley malts, hops, adjuncts, and other brewing essentials, designed to support beverage makers of all sizes and styles.

At RahrBSG, we value quality, innovation, and collaboration. We’re passionate about crafting excellence and fostering the growth of the craft beverage industry while upholding our family-owned values and commitment to sustainability. Join us and become part of a legacy dedicated to supporting the artistry and success of beverage makers worldwide.

added.title: Environmental Compliance Program Manager
added.description:
Job Description:

At Cambria, we take care of our people by offering a great workplace with excellent benefits. On the job, you will enjoy an exceptionally clean, climate controlled environment, paid lunch breaks, a shift differential pay for certain shifts and/or jobs, and Cambria uniforms and boots. Your health and future are covered with medical and dental insurance, life and disability coverage, and a 401(k) with an immediate company match. We also offer paid time off, paid holidays, an Employee Assistance Program, tuition reimbursement, opportunities for advancement, and an employee referral program.

Cambria is seeking an Environmental Compliance Program Manager to lead our facility’s environmental programs. This position will be responsible for managing the environmental performance of the site to ensure operations remain in full compliance with federal, state, and local regulations. The ideal candidate will possess deep technical expertise in air, storm water and regulated waste programs, combined with the project management skills necessary to drive continuous improvement and compliance initiatives.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Manage and maintain the site’s Title V Air Permit, ensuring all performance testing, monitoring, record-keeping, and reporting requirements are met.
Direct the management of Hazardous and Regulated Waste program, including inspections, training, waste stream characterization, profiling, labeling, storage, and manifesting. Primary point of contact for TSDF. Ensure compliance with RCRA/DOT regulations.
Maintain and manage the Industrial Storm water Program (SWPPP) including inspections, sampling/monitoring, program review, annual reporting and training.
Maintain and manage the Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) program including inspections, program review and training.
Lead the preparation and submission of annual regulatory reports, including Tier II (Emergency and Hazardous Chemical Inventory), TRI (Toxic Release Inventory), P2PR (Pollution Prevention Progress Report) and EIR (Emissions Inventory Report), Industrial Storm water annual and quarterly benchmark monitoring reports.
Act as the primary point of contact for regulatory agency inspections and inquiries.
Lead environmental compliance and improvement projects, ensuring effective implementation and support of environmental objectives
Oversee environmental training programs for staff on topics including hazardous waste handling, spill response, and permit requirements. Update content as needed.
Maintain a robust record-keeping system to ensure audit-readiness at all times
Development of and tracking of environmental Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s)
Track laws and regulations that may affect the organizations policies or practices and maintain a Compliance Calendar to identify internal and external compliance obligations
Conduct investigations, RCA and CAPA on Environmental/Chemical incidents

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Chemistry, or a related technical field.
Experience: 5–8 years of experience in industrial environmental compliance
Technical Knowledge: Deep working knowledge of EPA regulations (CAA, CWA, SPCC, RCRA, EPCRA, 40 CFR 60, Subpart WWWW and ZZZZ). Deep working knowledge of State of Minnesota environmental regulations.

Skills:

High attention to detail
Reliable and punctual
Ability to communicate effectively with all levels within the organization, and external vendors and regulators
Sense of urgency in work, demonstrated by consistent task completion
Capable of multitasking, and meet internal and regulatory deadlines
Work well both independently and with a team
Strong data management skills for complex reporting
Superior critical thinking and problem solving skills
Self-motivated; consistently demonstrates initiative
Rise to a challenge; “can-do” attitude
Generates results in a fast-paced, industrial manufacturing environment
Proven project management capability; ability to manage several projects at a time

Preferred Qualification/Certifications

Working knowledge of 40 CFR 60, Subpart WWWW and ZZZZ
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)
Hazwoper Certification

Managerial Responsibilities:
No

Travel Requirements:
Travel to local MN sites occasionally

Cambria Success Factors:

High attention to detail
Reliable and punctual
Direct communication
Sense of urgency in completing work
Capable of multitasking
Work well both independently and with a team
Self-motivated

Physical Requirements
:

Lift up to 50 lbs.
Push/pull 100 lbs.
Wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) provided by Cambria
Occasionally work in wet and/or humid conditions
Work in a non-climate controlled environment
Ability to walk industrial floor space, climb ladders/platforms and go up and down steps multiple times throughout shift as work dictates.
Bend over multiple times throughout shift

Task Based Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Requirements may include:

Steel toed boots
Hearing Protection
Safety glasses
Cut-proof gloves
Respirator
Face shield
High visibility vest
Chemical gloves

Cambria’s starting salary for this position is $97,594 - $135,170. Pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the target for new hires for the position. Individual pay is determined by several factors, including work location, job-related experience, and relevant education and/or training.

Cambria offers a competitive benefits package that encompasses Health and Dental Insurance, Paid Time Off, 7 paid Holidays , 401(k) plus matching, Discretionary Profit Sharing, Flexible Spending Account; Life, Supplemental Life, and Disability Insurance; Referral Program, Tuition Reimbursement, Employee Assistance Program, Employee Discount and Professional Development Assistance.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

At Cambria, dedication to philanthropy and our people is at the heart of who we are. We strive to make a meaningful difference in the world every day by prioritizing employee well-being and fostering inclusivity and empowerment. Under the banner of CambriaCares, our philanthropic endeavors show our commitment to our people and our community to uplift kids, support education, and contribute to a sustainable future.

For Additional Company Information, Please Visit Www.CambriaUSA.com

added.description:
Environmental Specialist

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Environmental Specialist for our
Lab & Onsite Support Services (Lab/OSS)
team. As an Environmental Specialist, you will support our clients on-site by managing their hazardous waste programs & projects, utilizing state & federal regulations.  
Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compliance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.    
This position reports to the Assistant Program Manager. This role is based on site at client locations in the   Collegeville, PA and King of Prussia, PA  area
. You will report out of our Norristown, PA office location.

We invite you to watch this video to discover more about the exciting responsibilities of an Environmental Specialist at Triumvirate Environmental.
CLICK HERE

Responsibilities:

Develop an understanding of OSHA regulations as well as Triumvirate’s Health and Safety practices 
Preparation of chemical and biological waste for shipment and disposal, including creation of all federal/state waste documents and managing the paperwork for the material. 
Safe handling of hazardous waste containers on client sites, as well as loading/unloading of waste from vehicles 
Will need to drive a Box truck for dropping off the waste within the same facility for a shorter distance during the day.
Occasionally will need to drive Forklift for shorter period of the day for moving waste within the warehouse at Client Facility
Conduct safety equipment and hazardous waste inspections. 
Occasionally perform and document Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) audits for clients. 
Deliver Exceptional Customer Service: Champion our commitment to the WOW! by providing outstanding support and innovative solutions to our clients 
Develop a high-level of state and federal regulatory expertise ensuring our client’s compliance needs are met (e.g RCRA, DOT, and OSHA) 
Conduct spill response measures, including the assessment of the spills and cleanup efforts 
Rotating on-call responsibilities as part of our Emergency Response team

Basic Requirements
:  
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in the hazardous-waste industry, or relevant military experience 
Ability to work as a member of a team as well as individually 
Must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication abilities to effectively interact with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional exchanges of information 
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues, develop solutions, and implement strategies to achieve positive outcomes 
Skilled in building strong, positive relationships with clients and colleagues 
Ability to work overtime on a regular basis 
Must be willing to work flexible hours within the work week (Monday through Friday) 
Ability to complete a 2 to 3 year professional advancement program in hazardous waste management 
The Environmental Specialist frequently handles hazardous chemicals and biological waste and is responsible for putting on and taking off personal protective equipment. This role is considered safety-sensitive 
Must be able to report to Norristown , PA  office within 1 hour during Emergency Response rotating shifts 
Valid US driver’s license 
Must have a reliable form of transportation 
Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC) 
Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment 
Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship 
Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis 

Preferred Requirements:

Prior relevant industry experience 
Prior successful experience in a customer service role 
Active HAZWOPER 24 or 40 hour certification 
Willingness to obtain Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) 

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!

added.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist
added.description:
Environmental Compliance Specialist I – NASA Glenn Research Center

Ready to take your environmental career to new heights? Join HSG in supporting NASA's mission!

We're looking for an Environmental Compliance Specialist to support environmental programs at NASA Glenn's Armstrong Test Facility in Ohio. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience across hazardous waste management, stormwater, wastewater, spill prevention, and environmental compliance while contributing to the important work happening at NASA.

If you're passionate about environmental protection, enjoy hands-on problem-solving, and are ready to make an impact, we'd love to hear from you! Apply today and take the next step in your career with HSG!

General Description

Herndon Solutions Group (HSG) is seeking an Environmental Compliance Specialist I to serve as the on-site, multi-media environmental compliance resource at the NASA Glenn Research Center Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility (GRC-ATF) in Erie County, Ohio. The Specialist administers day-to-day compliance coordination across hazardous and regulated waste; petroleum, oil, and lubricant (POL) and tanks; spill preparedness and response; and stormwater and wastewater. The position evaluates site conditions, integrates requirements across environmental media, supports functional-area leads with inspections, field work, sampling, records, and reporting, and tracks ATF compliance issues through resolution. The Specialist supports Lewis Field when cross-site workload or continuity needs arise and reports to the designated HSG Project Manager/Site Lead. 

How You Will Fulfill Your Mission

Conduct and document environmental compliance inspections of hazardous and universal waste accumulation areas, used oil, POL/tanks, stormwater systems, wastewater operations, construction activities, and other assigned areas.
Serve as the primary on-site lead for the environmental compliance program for regulated waste, POL/tank, spills, stormwater, and wastewater, including permit requirements, inspections, monitoring, recordkeeping, deliverables, and corrective actions to identify compliance risks, recommend priorities, and support program improvements. 
Identify deficiencies, communicate findings, and recommend corrective actions based on an evaluation of regulatory significance, environmental risk, and operational impact. 
Support regulated and controlled waste management activities at ATF, including generator coordination, waste determinations, accumulation-area management, shipment documentation, sampling coordination, and cradle-to-grave recordkeeping including evaluation of waste characterization information and recommendations concerning appropriate management and disposal approaches. 
Support Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC), spill prevention, and POL/tank programs through inspections, inventory verification, spill response guide updates, alarm and event documentation, closure or maintenance support, and corrective-action tracking. 
Maintain ATF spill readiness and response activities, including initial assessments, containment coordination, sampling, waste management, documentation, reporting support, and post-incident follow-up. 
Support stormwater and wastewater permit compliance through site inspections, outfall screening, wet- and dry-weather monitoring, construction and post-construction best management practice (BMP) inspections, sampling coordination, discharge monitoring data reviews, equipment checks, reporting inputs, and maintenance of applicable plans and records.
Coordinate with laboratories and functional-area leads on field sampling plans, chain of custody, data quality, analytical results, and follow-up actions. 
Assist with identifying recurring compliance issues, evaluating potential environmental risks, and recommending practical improvements to procedures and environmental controls.
Support environmental audits, regulatory inspections, investigations, emergency drills, project reviews, meetings, and field activities, providing accurate ATF records and site knowledge. 
Coordinate closely with the Hazardous Waste Specialists at Lewis Field and the applicable waste, POL, stormwater, wastewater, and spill response functional leads to ensure consistent practices across both GRC locations. 
Track assigned environmental compliance issues and corrective actions through closure, escalating potential compliance concerns and matters requiring specialist review, Government approval, or regulatory coordination to the appropriate personnel.
Support emergency spill response activities at Lewis Field and ATF on an on-call/as needed basis and as coordinated by the Site Lead.

Why We Value You

You are able to work independently and show a high level of initiative and attention to detail.
You have a consistent character and do not yield to pressure to compromise or cut corners.
You have a strong ability to communicate effectively with superiors, colleagues, and customers by clearly expressing your intent and understanding the focus and purpose of the conversation while allowing each person to get their point across.
You are open to new ideas and innovations and can create modifications or changes in yourself to adapt or suit a new environment/situation.
You have faith in your own ideas and ability to be successful.
You hold yourself to the highest standard and work to inspire your team to produce quality work.

Specific Knowledge/Certification Requirements

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in environmental compliance, regulatory documentation, environmental monitoring, or related technical activities, including the ability to evaluate technical information and identify potential compliance concerns.
RCRA Hazardous Waste Management training and required refreshers or the ability to obtain prior to beginning field work.
DOT Hazardous Materials Ground Shipper training and required refreshers. 
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training and required refreshers. 
A Valid driver’s license and ability to obtain and maintain required NASA facility access. 

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry, biology, geology, occupational safety, or related discipline. 
Three or more years of multi-media environmental compliance experience at an industrial, research, aerospace, government, or similarly regulated facility. 
Experience with Ohio EPA requirements, NPDES permits, SPCC requirements, RCRA generator standards, construction stormwater controls, and environmental data and reporting systems. 
Ohio BUSTR Class A/B or Class C operator training, stormwater inspection credentials, or other applicable media-specific qualifications. 

Working Conditions

This is primarily an on-site position at the designated reporting location, with routine support at the other GRC location as operational needs require, including local travel between GRC-ATF and Lewis Field. 
Supports GRC core business hours. 
Must be able to work independently at GRC-ATF, including at remote site locations. 
Work may be performed in office, laboratory, industrial, warehouse, utility, construction, outdoor, and active facility environments. 
Must be able to lift, carry, or move 30 pounds or more; climb stairs; bend, stoop, twist, and reach; and stand or walk for two hours or more at one time. 
Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment and work in varying weather and site conditions. 
Conducts field inspections and sampling and provides limited hands-on support when needed to evaluate or coordinate compliance. Such work is incidental to the position’s primary compliance-administration duties. 
Must be able to participate in assigned emergency readiness and response coverage, including after-hours support when required.
